units.translation: αὑτοῦ [himself, herself, itself] reflexive pronoun, especially when joined with αὐτός [self] and its oblique cases, sometimes used for ἐμαυτοῦ [myself] and σεαυτοῦ [yourself]: on which I have spoken in Lexicon Sophocleum p. 74.
i.e. ὑπ' ἀλλήλων [by one another].
For ἐμαυτοῦ [myself]
For σεαυτοῦ [yourself]
Of the trisyllabic form ἑαυτοῦ [himself, herself, itself] there are three examples in Aeschylus in a single play,
himself against himself, of empty-minded counsels.

αὐτόχθον᾿ ὃν [which native] Blomfield. Since αὐτόχθων [native] means one born in the very land, the poet seemed to need another form if he was to say one who suffered something together with his own land. Scholefield also saw this. Lobeck defends the form of the word. Paralip. p. 202.” HERM.
